sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
Closure, Chief Engineer of Rhodes Island, takes to the frontline in person as a Vanguard!

Arriving at the front lines alongside her: a toolkit, drones, snacks, and all the engineering problems in her head still waiting to be solved.

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A blank sheet of paper. You recognize it as the stock she prints her coupons on, and can't help itching to give it a try.

sections.title: Profile
sections.text:
Closure, Rhodes Island's Chief Engineer and head of the Procurement Department, who also oversees the affairs of several other departments.

I'll be waiting for you all over in Procurement. If you want to get to know me, do you really need to read my file?
—Closure

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Closure shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.14u/L
Closure frequently handles Originium industrial products of all kinds, and her Blood Originium-Crystal Density is on the high side. However, the Oripathy protection measures she takes are rigorous and reliable, so all things considered, the risk of infection is low.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
This document is paid content and is currently locked. Please contact Closure to purchase access.

If you actually pay, she'll hand the money back and then let you read the text. If you track Closure down—assuming you can catch her—she'll cheerfully admit that charging a fee violates Rhodes Island's regulations, and then let you read the text.
And if you neither pay nor find her, yet still end up reading the text, she'll turn up behind you of her own accord, interrogate you about how you managed it, and then spend a few nights sealing the hole shut.
——■■■

(Whereupon the head of HR readily told you the several methods she knew for getting around the lock. You picked one of them and duly gained access to the locked content. During your reading, however, a drone-shaped desktop pet appeared on your screen. It could not be closed, and every so often it would pop up a little speech bubble reading 'Foul play!' or 'Pay your fine!' and the like... Yet Closure never did sever the connection between you and this file.)

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
There is no doubt that Closure is one of the old-timers with the longest tenure on Rhodes Island.
Generally speaking, old-timers tend to develop memorable quirks—take Warfarin's late-night Medical Department horror stories. By comparison, Closure is fairly ordinary. What she does rarely goes beyond the purview of a Chief Engineer and head of Procurement.
It is worth noting that during Kal'tsit's absence, Closure additionally had to render the final judgment on important decisions for every Rhodes Island department (the Medical Department usually excepted). That burden did lighten after Kal'tsit's return, yet a considerable portion of it still rests on her shoulders for one reason or another. Closure's own attitude toward this is decidedly conflicted: the workload of the Engineering Department and Procurement alone already looks heavy enough even to an outsider, but beneath that glib exterior, an old-timer's sense of responsibility makes it hard for her to toss those burdens back onto a Kal'tsit who has only just returned.
Still, why Closure of all people became one of Rhodes Island's old-timers, and why she holds a sense of responsibility toward Rhodes Island so at odds with her image, remains an interesting question. We could of course trace it back to the day Theresa opened the door to her room; we could credit her fierce curiosity for driving her to follow in the footsteps of Babel, of Theresa, and even of the Doctor; we could attribute it to the deep bonds formed over long years alongside the members of Babel and Rhodes Island; and part of the reason is plainly that being at Rhodes Island grants her access to no end of advanced technology the average person has never even heard of...

Haven't you already gone through all the reasons?
—Closure

...All of that holds true, and yet none of it quite explains where she stands today. Emotional ties and access to the latest technology are certainly enough to keep her at Rhodes Island, but they hardly seem enough to make someone so plainly disinclined to hard work take such evident pleasure in the work of a pharmaceutical company—especially work that is, in truth, intensely repetitive.

Ugh, what a pain.
—Closure

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
Kazdel's infrastructure remains rather incomplete even today, and its newly laid intercity network has yet to reach widespread adoption. Which inevitably raises the question: in that far more chaotic and desolate era, did Kazdel really contain an information kingdom for Closure to run wild in?
Closure's answer to that was: 'If there isn't one, just build one yourself.'
The reality was not so breezy, of course. The Kazdel of that time offered no soil whatsoever for an intercity network, and there was essentially only one way for the Sarkaz to get their hands on electronics: taking them from the Sankta.
What the average Sarkaz wanted most was, naturally, a patron firearm, followed by foreign currencies, Originium Ingots, and precious metals, and after that anything edible, drinkable, or otherwise of practical use. Most advanced electronics were, frankly, baffling contraptions to them: heavy, complicated, and worth nothing once taken apart. Some, however, would haul the stuff back to Kazdel to hawk it in the spirit of salvage, and that was what gave the Sarkaz inside the city their chance to encounter electronics at all. Closure was among the very first to get her hands on them.
But stepping outside meant facing family she was on strained terms with, and all the strange knowledge and new discoveries filling her head had no one to be shared with. Closure in those days was likely hungrier for conversation than at any other point in her life... until she managed to reach another circuitry enthusiast nearby on a particular wavelength. What followed needs no telling.
Even recently, the engineers laying intercity network infrastructure in Kazdel still turn up homemade base stations and repeaters tucked into every odd corner—all of them the handiwork of Closure and her friends back in the day. Closure handled the design and the communications from her attic, while her friends did the installing on-site.

A quick aside: in the sentence 'back then I tinkered with circuits up in the attic,' the most important piece of information isn't the tinkering—it's the attic. Being able to afford a house with an attic, where locking the door shut out nearly every distraction—honestly, in the Kazdel of that time, that was lucky to the point of luxury.
An aside to the aside: the first piece of electronics I ever got my hands on had been modified by the Sankta it was taken from... by the Sankta who was killed for it. I wanted to talk with that person. I wanted it for a very, very long time.
That person shouldn't have died like that. Neither should the Sarkaz who died killing them.
—Closure

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
Having successfully built a little circle of technological pioneers in Kazdel, Closure and her friends soon faced their first rift—what they had already done, what they could do, and what they might one day do was more than enough to be traded for money across Kazdel and most of Terra. And a great, great deal of money at that.
A few friends short on cash proposed cashing in. A circle that loose could hardly stop them, and those friends promptly became hot commodities in the Scar Market. Later still, some who simply couldn't stand conditions in Kazdel left for distant lands, and with Kazdel's punishing rate of population turnover on top of that, Closure found herself keeping to herself again, with only a handful of friends she knew inside and out—or believed she did—left to talk to.
It was also during this period that the notoriety of a certain vandal began to spread through Kazdel. This character would hack indiscriminately into any database she could get into (most of them set up for someone or other by her former friends), any server (a rarity among rarities), even personal terminals taken by force—sometimes leaving nothing but a trace before moving on, sometimes tearing the place apart as if venting. Outside the attic, meanwhile, Closure's family had, unusually, begun to worry whether this wayward little troublemaker had suffered some sort of mental blow lately—and their worry wasn't misplaced, as it happens.
Only much, much later did Closure realize that what she had longed for back then was something Columbia calls the 'open-source spirit'—something utterly at odds with her identity as a Vampire.
Closure long ago desensitized herself to being a Vampire and to what 'a Vampire ought to be like.' Ask her now and she will plainly rattle off the Vampires she doesn't dislike (Warfarin), doesn't much dislike (Entelechia), does dislike (Duq'arael), and would rather die than meet (her own parents). Before she worked it all out, though, her identity as a Vampire really was a question that troubled her for a long time—why had she been born into a race that chases 'purity' and 'perfection,' and marks its ranks with words as emotionally loaded as 'filth' and 'degeneracy'?
Software development requires trial and error; engineering construction must allow for margins of error and redundancy; and between her and that first group of friends, nothing was off-limits at all. For her, merely recalling the whole Vampire doctrine mid-conversation was enough to set her teeth on edge. That is why she wanted open source—a place where anyone could freely take, freely study, and freely contribute; or at the very least, she wanted to create the conditions for such a place.
Perhaps, for her, this was the most immediate understanding of what it means to 'break the shackles of tradition.'
Barriers between races, discrimination born of differences in seniority, hierarchies built on bloodline... every one of these was a shackle of tradition binding her, and not one of them went unbroken by her.
From that perspective, her reason for walking alongside us has never once changed from the very beginning.

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
This part is genuinely paid content!
I said it's paid content. You're really going to read it anyway?
...Hmph.

(You had expected to uncover some tremendous secret, but what appears on the screen hardly sets the pulse racing. It is a long reading list, spanning fields as broad as pharmaceutical manufacturing, precision industry, civil engineering, and interior design. You know that every one of them is something she has read. No one starts out an engineering expert in every field—not even a Vampire as unorthodox as her—and Closure has in all likelihood spent no small sum on these journals, magazines, and treatises, or at least on their digital editions. Further down there is also all the laboratory equipment she has purchased. That really is a hefty expense, you think, and with a sigh you drag the list straight to the bottom.)

Payment successful...

（？）

...You have been charged 180,000 LMD via ZOOT Express Pay.
